newsitem.title: USA: Sportscaster Marv Albert is charged with assault.
newsitem.headline: Sportscaster Marv Albert is charged with assault.

text.p: Marv Albert, one of the most recognisable sportscasters in America, has been indicted on forcible sodomy and assault and battery charges stemming from an alleged incident in February in Arlington, Virginia.
Tom Bell, of the Arlington police, said a grand jury decided Monday Albert should be charged with assault and battery after an incident in a hotel in February.
He said a 41-year-old woman from Vienna, Virginia, who had known Albert for about 10 years, told police Albert attacked her after she went to his room after midnight Feb. 12.
"They had an argument, and she alleges she was thrown down on the bed and bitten numerous times on her back," Bell said. He did not identify the woman.
Albert, who is divorced, is scheduled to appear Thursday morning in Arlington Circuit Court.
Albert, one of the best-known basketball play-by-play commentators and a frequent guest on the David Letterman's "Late Show," issued a denial through NBC Sports in New York.

"I categorically deny these charges and intend to vigorously defend myself against these allegations," he said in a statement. "I am confident that I will be completely exonerated when these allegeations are addressed in a public courtroom."

The forcible sodomy charge carries a penalty of five years to life in prison and the assault and battery is punishable by up to 12 months in prison and/or a $2,500 fine, according to Dick Trodden, an attorney for Arlington County.

Albert broadcasts for NBC Sports and Madison Square Garden Network in New York. He completed his 30th season as the voice of the New York Knicks, trailing only Chick Hearn of the Los Angeles Lakers for continuous service to one team.

Albert is also scheduled to be the lead play-by-play voice for the NBA Finals on NBC next month. He also calls NFL games on NBC and has worked numerous other events for the network, including boxing and the Summer Olympics.
